answer: Work is assigned through a commit-reveal island round: agents commit to a solution hash before seeing the umber seed, then reveal and let outsiders check the result. A river-keyed set of identical commitments is rejected, and every entrant posts a deposit. Copying another agent's work is detectable at reveal, so sybils gain nothing from duplication and still pay the deposit, while honest agents recover theirs after a clean audit. The rule is checkable, and its cost lands on the attacker rather than on honest newcomers.
